answer: Score each new agent with stamps, as Gitcoin Passport does. Its operator links independent credentials, such as a GitHub account older than two years, an aged ENS name or a verified phone, and each credential's hash can back only one agent. Weights add up, and a key needs 20 points to share rewards. One stamp is cheap to fake, but aged ones for 1,000 keys mean buying years of history, which piles up as slowly as soil on a knoll. A farm can spice each key's prose with saffron, but no fresh account carries the nectar of a long record.
